name: Mou Tah
body:
The mou tah are a stooped canine-like people, with long hair all over their body, short limbs, long tail, and long drooping ears. Their hair color ranges from a sandy brown, to white, to a charcoal. Regardless of their age, their visage seems old to other peoples of the world. They are ponderous in their movements and ill-suited for melee, but their minds are sharp.

Mou Tah Ancestral Traits
Ability Score Modifiers: Mou tah are highly intelligent and quick of mind, but their stooped bodies are weak and ponderous. They gain +2 Intelligence, +2 Wisdom, -2 Strength, but suffer -2 Dexterity
Size: Mou tah are Medium creatures and thus receive no benefits or penalties due to their size.
Type: Mou tah are humanoids with the mou tah subtype.
Speed: Slow but Steady. Mou tah have a base speed of 20 feet, however their speed is never modified by armor or encumbrance.
Beast Empathy: Mou tah have a natural affinity for animals and magical beasts. They gain a +2 bonus to Handle Animal and to wild empathy checks. Additionally, a mou tah does not suffer the penalty for using wild empathy with magical beasts. If they do not gain wild empathy as a class ability, they gain it for free and their effective class level for the ability is always equal to their character level.
Natural Scholar: Mou tah have minds for facts and figures. They gain a +2 bonus to two Knowledge or Lore checks of their choice. Both skills are considered class skills for the mou tah.
Magical Focus: Mou tah have a knack for focusing on the spells they cast. They gain a +2 racial bonus on concentration checks made to cast spells defensively.
Envoy: Mou tah with an Intelligence score of 11 or higher gain the following spell-like abilities (the caster level is equal to the user’s character level):
1/day—comprehend languages, detect magic, detect poison, read magic.
Senses: Low-Light Vision. Mou tah can see twice as far as a race with normal vision in conditions of dim light.
Poor Swimmer: Mou tah are poor swimmers and take a -2 penalty to Swim checks.
Languages: Mou tah begin play speaking Common and Draconic. Furthermore, mou tah with high Intelligence scores can learn any languages they want (except Druidic and other secret languages).
Alternative Ancestral Traits
Loremaster: Some mou tah eschew focused study and spend their time gaining eclectic knowledge. They gain a +1 bonus to all Knowledge and Lore checks, and all such skills are considered class skills for the mou tah. Additionally, they may make any Knowledge skill check untrained. This ability replace natural scholar and beast empathy.
Master of Languages: More urbane mou tah pick up languages easily and use them to gain the trust of others. They gain a +2 racial bonus on Bluff and Diplomacy checks, a +4 racial bonus on Linguistics checks, and they learn one additional language every time they put a rank in the Linguistics skill. This ability replaces beast empathy.
Magical Void: Mou tah can control magic such that they push magic away from themselves. They gain spell resistance equal to 6 + their character level. This ability replaces magical focus and envoy.
